newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Delta Gold says dividends will go on.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Delta Gold says dividends will go on.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Wednesday that it was now in a position to continue paying dividends to shareholders.
Delta earlier on Wednesday announced a maiden half year dividend of a 1.5 cents a share.
"Our ability to continue paying a dividend is sustainable," Fiona Robertson, general manager of finance, told Reuters.
Robertson said the company's cash needs can be met in the foreseeable future, enabling it to pay dividends.
"We can see that we are easily able to meet our ongoing exploration, forecast mine development and mine feasibility study needs," Robertson said.
Delta, which mines gold in Western Australia and holds a 33 percent interest in the Hartley platinum mine project is Zimbabwe, earlier on Wednesday posted a half-year net profit A$10.4 million.
Delta's current gold hedging programme left the company unexposed for the remainder of 1996/97 (July/June) if the gold price fell below US$347 an ounce, Vanderspuy said.
A total of 250,000 ounces of gold is forward sold at an average price of A$688, he said.
In Zimbabwe, Vanderspuy said slower-than-expected development of the Hartley mine meant the project would not reach full production of 180,000 tonnes before late 1998.
Delta and 67 percent owner, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, previously had hoped to see the mine at full throttle by September 1998, he said.
"It's not a technical problem," Vanderspuy said.
Vanderspuy said Delta's exploration budget had nearly doubled to A$23 million since the start of 1996/97, reflecting the company's aim of boosting its gold production.

About A$17 million was earmarked for advanced exploration projects underway by Delta, including the Granny Smith and Kanowna Belle gold mines in Western Australia and the Golden Feather prospect, Vanderspuy said.
About A$5.7 million was to be spent on exploration in Zimbabwe, Vanderspuy said.

Profits before tax and and abnormal items of A$11.6 million for the six months ended December 31, represented a solid performance considering the lower gold gold prices that prevailed during the period, Vanderspuy said.
Delta gold sales over the six month period averaged A$121 an ounce above the spot price, he said.
